sources.title: Mehryar Mohri, Afshin Rostamizadeh, and Ameet Talwalkar, Foundations of Machine Learning, 2nd ed. (MIT Press, 2018)
sources.locator: Complete 505-page second-edition PDF. Chapter 3 §3.1, Definitions 3.1–3.2, Theorem 3.3 and complete proof, printed pp. 30–33; Chapter 5 §5.4, Lemma 5.7 and complete proof, printed pp. 93–94.

contents.name: Definitions 3.1–3.2: empirical and expected one-sided Rademacher complexity with 1/m normalization
Theorem 3.3 full proof: ghost sample, one-sided symmetrization, bounded differences and the 2 R_m bound
Theorem 3.3 and complete proof: expected and empirical one-sided generalization bounds with exact constants
Lemma 5.7 and complete proof: coordinatewise Lipschitz contraction, factor L, with no zero-at-zero condition
Theorem 3.3 uniform deviation used in the two-deviation ERM comparison
Theorem 3.5 binary-classification specialization
contents.reason: The assigned claims are for general [0,1]-valued loss classes and do not add a binary-classification specialization.

contents.name: Theorem 3.7 Massart finite-class complexity bound
contents.reason: The finite-class example is an exact two-function sign calculation and does not use Massart's lemma.

sources.title: Peter L. Bartlett and Shahar Mendelson, Rademacher and Gaussian Complexities: Risk Bounds and Structural Results, Journal of Machine Learning Research 3 (2002), 463–482
sources.locator: Complete 20-page JMLR PDF. Definition 2; Theorem 5 and Appendix B proof; Theorems 7–9; Theorem 12 and proof; Appendix A, proof of Lemma 3; Appendix B, proof of Theorem 5.

contents.name: Definition 2: absolute-value Rademacher complexity with the paper's 2/m scaling
contents.reason: Used as an independent comparison; its absolute-value and 2/m convention is explicitly kept distinct.

contents.name: Theorem 5 and Appendix B proof: high-probability risk bounds
contents.reason: Read as an independent comparison; the exact normalization and constants in the authored claim come from Mohri's one-sided convention.

contents.name: Theorem 8 and complete proof: general bounded-loss Rademacher risk bound
contents.reason: Read as an independent ghost-sample and sign-symmetrization treatment with the paper's separate normalization.

contents.name: Theorem 8 and complete proof: bounded-loss high-probability risk bound
contents.reason: Used for comparison only; the local ERM excess calculation is proved directly from the exact current uniform-deviation supplier.

contents.name: Theorem 12(4): absolute-value Lipschitz contraction
contents.reason: It assumes the scalar map vanishes at zero and uses an absolute supremum with factor 2L, unlike the assigned one-sided factor-L claim.

contents.name: Theorem 7 margin bound
contents.reason: Its margin-loss conclusion is outside the assigned scope; no margin claim is authored.

contents.name: Theorem 1 introductory display
contents.reason: The display omits a confidence term and is explicitly excluded by the controlling plan.

contents.name: Theorem 9 McDiarmid statement and Appendix A proof of Lemma 3
contents.reason: Read for context; the assigned concentration proof uses the complete local McDiarmid supplier, and no discrepancy comparison claim is authored.
